summary.headline: Aequs FY26 revenue rose 33% to INR12,304 million with a record Q4 of INR3,671 million; FY27 guides 45-50% consolidated growth and consumer EBITDA breakeven by Q4 FY27.
summary.overview: FY26 consolidated revenue grew 33% to INR12,304 million and EBITDA grew 43% to INR1,545 million (13% margin), but full-year PAT was a loss of INR1,133 million. Q4 was the highest-ever quarter at INR3,671 million revenue, yet EBITDA margin fell to 9% as consumer electronics capacity, commissioned in Q3, carried full depreciation and fixed costs at about 23% utilisation. Aerospace carried the year (revenue INR10,464 million, EBITDA margin about 27%), while consumer EBITDA loss widened to INR783 million. Management also announced two state MoUs for about INR4,756 crores of multi-year capex, the CFO's exit at end-June 2026, and the loss of Hasbro volumes offset by a Mattel long-term agreement.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR10,464 million (+27%), EBITDA INR2,813 million (+76%); Q4 revenue INR3,040 million (+29%), EBITDA INR1,010 million. Portfolio grew to 5,654 SKUs (+26% YoY, 433 added in Q4); order book USD 889 million.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue INR1,840 million (+84%), EBITDA loss INR783 million. Capacity utilisation at 23%, targeted at 40-50% by FY27 year-end; FY27 consumer revenue growth guided at 125-150%.

segments.name: Consumer durables JV (50:50)
segments.commentary: Not consolidated within the consumer segment, per management; no revenue split across consumer verticals was disclosed.

guidance_outlook: FY27 aerospace revenue growth of 25-30% with segment EBITDA margin held at about 20% (excluding other income and unallocated corporate costs, per Q&A).
FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 45-50%; management expects operational EBITDA to double.
Consumer EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27; long-term consumer EBITDA goal of about 20%, with 18-20% expected at roughly 75-80% utilisation.
Consolidated PAT expected to reach breakeven by H1 FY28; depreciation keeps PAT negative for much of FY27.
FY27 capex of about INR500 crores in consumer and about INR160 crores in aerospace; PLI eligibility begins in FY27 (none booked in FY26). Interest expense expected to fall versus FY26.
Consumer gross block about INR830 crores; asset turn expected near 1.5x at peak; INR2,000 crore consumer turnover on about INR1,330 crore gross block was indicated as closer to FY29.
capex_capacity: Installed capacity at 4.70 million annualised machining and moulding hours; 2.22 million sq ft across Belagavi, Hubballi and Koppal in India, plus Cholet (France) and Paris, Texas (US).
Fleet of 434 CNC machines and 179 moulding machines at FY26 close.

MoU with Tamil Nadu (Feb 2026): INR1,900 crores over 10 years for a 250-acre aerospace and defence park at Hosur (SIPCOT Shoolagiri), described as India's first fully vertically integrated aero engine and landing gear ecosystem.
MoU with Karnataka (Mar 2026): INR2,856 crores over five years across Belagavi (aerospace precision) and Hubballi (consumer capacity).
Funding: FY27 capex to be financed through borrowings plus some internal accruals; a breakdown was deferred offline.
Consumer capacity utilisation at 23%; management said the customer relationship requires scaling and that alternates would be sought otherwise.
demand_pricing: Hasbro informed Aequs it has revised its manufacturing and sourcing strategy and will stop raising purchase orders; management said overall consumer growth will not be impacted.
Long-term agreement signed with Mattel; management expects Mattel volumes to absorb the Hasbro capacity impact.
Aerospace order book USD 889 million, roughly 8-9x FY26 aerospace revenue per analyst framing; management is moving into engine and landing gear components, with engine revenue starting FY28.
About 93-94% of revenue is USD-linked including deemed exports.
Aluminium/steel and titanium lead times cited at 65-75 weeks and 52 weeks respectively; buffer stock raised to about 125% of quarterly needs from about 70%.
Plastics prices rose in the quarter but are passed through to consumer customers under back-to-back agreements.

qa_highlights.question: Planned capex by segment for FY27-28, Mattel ramp after Hasbro, PLI income?
qa_highlights.answer: Aerospace capex about INR160 crores and consumer about INR500 crores for FY27. Mattel LTA signed. No PLI income booked in FY26; FY27 is the first eligible year.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of the West Asia crisis on margins and working capital?
qa_highlights.answer: Management saw no significant margin impact in Q4; the working capital build reflects inventory held 4-6 weeks ahead, expected for about two more quarters. Air freight is up 6-8 days and sea freight 5-6 weeks.

qa_highlights.question: Reconciling FY26 aerospace 27% margin with 20% FY27 guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: The 27% is segment EBITDA including other income and before unallocated corporate costs; the like-for-like operating margin is about 20%.

qa_highlights.question: Why add consumer capex with utilisation at 23%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the customer wants a meaningful share of India requirements; the capex is customer-driven and the asset base will ramp, with utilisation targeted at 40-50%.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer revenue potential from INR500 crore capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided utilisation to 50% and consumer growth of about 125% this year; no revenue figure was given for the capex.

qa_highlights.question: Long-term aerospace growth beyond FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited a multi-year opportunity at 20-plus% growth and said the engine component contribution starts in FY28, with FY27 growth predominantly from aerostructures.

qa_highlights.question: Depreciation and interest run-rate for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 depreciation was about INR45-46 crores, plus additions from capex; interest expense expected to decline versus FY26.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer margin path and steady-state utilisation?
qa_highlights.answer: Margins are driven by utilisation; 18-20% margins are expected around 75-80% utilisation.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer funding for the planned capex?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex to be funded by borrowings and some internal accruals; a breakdown was deferred offline.

risks_watch: Consumer utilisation must rise from 23% to 40-50% in FY27 to reach EBITDA breakeven in Q4 FY27; ramp slippage would extend losses.
Hasbro's exit from purchase orders; Mattel volume ramp is not yet quantified.
CFO Dinesh Iyer steps down at end-June 2026; replacement not yet named, Harish Bang is interim contact.
Working capital at 151 days and elevated inventory for about two quarters due to logistics disruption; China-sourced equipment supply constraints.
Rising debt-funded capex (about INR660 crores in FY27 across both segments) may weigh on balance sheet and PAT recovery.
Consumer electronics yield and quality data not disclosed, citing customer confidentiality.
summary.management_tone: Confident on aerospace growth and margins, and on consumer breakeven timing, but evasive on consumer funding breakdown, yield metrics and the Hasbro impact, which were deferred or answered at a high level.
key_quotes: Third, move our consumer EBITDA to break even by Q4 FY27, which will be a major inflection point for our consolidated profitability.
As utilization improves from 23% to our 40% to 50% target for FY27, the depreciation and fixed costs will be absorbed across higher volumes, and margins will recover sharply.
While this decision was unexpected, it will not impact the overall growth of the business.

We're also actively moving up the value chain into landing gear and engine components, where our integrated forging, machining, and surface treatment capabilities deliver significant competitive advantages.

growth.why: Management guides FY27 consolidated revenue growth of 45-50% and aerospace growth of 25-30% backed by a 1,000+ USD million order book (USD 889 million), while consumer growth of 125-150% rests on utilisation rising from 23% to 40-50% and about INR500 crore capex, with backing shown mainly as a qualitative plan rather than specific contracts for consumer volumes.
